name: Sooji Halwa
steps: Measure all ingredients before starting, since the mixture thickens quickly. Heat the water separately and keep it hot; chop the cashews for the finishing step.
Melt ghee in a heavy pan over medium-low heat. Add semolina and roast for 8–10 minutes, stirring and scraping the base, until fragrant and evenly light golden.
Lower the heat and carefully add hot water in small additions, stirring continuously. Keep your hand and face clear of steam and splashes as the water meets the hot mixture.
Stir until the water is absorbed and the semolina swells. Break up any lumps against the side of the pan; the grains should soften before adding sugar.
Add sugar and cardamom and stir well. The mixture will loosen at first, then thicken as you cook for another 3–5 minutes over low heat.
Stop when the halwa is smooth and moves together as a soft mass, rather than becoming dry and crumbly. Finish with chopped cashews and serve warm.
tips: Add water carefully; the hot mixture splutters.
substitutions: Any substitution changes the recipe: recheck allergies, Jain rules and quantities.
notes: Prices are sample ingredient-cost assumptions. Replace with supplier rates before procurement.
